title: Consistency of Scale-Dependent Gravitational Response in EFC: Numerical Regime Transition Test
description: Numerical test showing that a single relativistic EFC action yields suppressed linear growth (μ < 1) on cosmological scales while remaining compatible with enhanced gravity (μ > 1) in the non-linear Newtonian/galactic regime. The scale-dependent stiffness response R(k) ∝ k^-4 drives a smooth transition, recovers GR at high k, reproduces the survival valley (μ ≈ 0.94, η > 1, Σ > 1), and achieves fσ8 consistency with Δχ² = −0.03 versus ΛCDM.

key_results.main_finding: A single EFC action yields μ < 1 in linear cosmology and is compatible with μ > 1 in the non-linear Newtonian regime via a smooth k^-4 stiffness-driven transition, reproducing the survival valley and GR recovery.

sealed_predictions.statement: Cluster-scale transition with μeff ≈ 1.1 and Σeff ≈ 1.2 near k ~ 0.3 h/Mpc in the non-linear regime.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: DES Y6 and Euclid cluster weak lensing and dynamics jointly finding |μeff−1| < 0.03 and |Σeff−1| < 0.03 at k ~ 0.2–0.4 h/Mpc with systematics-controlled analyses.

sealed_predictions.statement: No μ > 1 in the linear perturbative regime (k ≲ 0.1 h/Mpc): the EFT structure forbids linear-scale enhancement.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Combined CMB, BAO, and RSD analyses detecting μ(k) > 1 at k ≲ 0.1 h/Mpc and z ≲ 1 at >3σ significance.

kill_criteria: KC1: Robust detection (≥3σ, multi-probe CMB+lensing+RSD) of μ(k) > 1 in the linear regime at k ≲ 0.1 h/Mpc and z ≲ 1.
KC2: Joint weak-lensing and RSD constraints exclude the predicted survival valley by finding Σ(k) ≤ 1 and η(k) ≈ 1 at k ≈ 0.02–0.1 h/Mpc with ≥3σ significance.
KC3: Scale dependence inconsistent with R(k) ∝ k^-4: growth and lensing data jointly reject any k^-4-like suppression (best-fit power n ≥ −2) over 0.02 < k < 0.2 h/Mpc at ≥3σ.
KC4: Failure of GR recovery at high k in the linear regime: persistent linear-scale deviations with μ−1 or η−1 ≳ 0.02 detected at k ≳ 0.3 h/Mpc after non-linear marginalization.

KC5: Non-linear (cluster-scale) tests rule out enhancement: DES/Euclid find |μeff−1| < 0.03 and |Σeff−1| < 0.03 over 0.2 < k < 0.5 h/Mpc with S/N ≥ 5, contradicting the predicted μeff ≈ 1.1 and Σeff ≈ 1.2.

KC6: Large-scale structure growth (fσ8) shows a significant degradation vs ΛCDM with Δχ² ≥ +9 for all EFC parameter combinations consistent with other constraints, indicating no viable parameter space.

abstract: First numerical consistency test of the EFC regime transition. The same relativistic action produces μ < 1 (suppressed growth) in the linear cosmological regime and is compatible with μ > 1 (enhanced gravity) in the non-linear galactic regime. Using μ(k) = (1+ε_F)/(F(1+R(k))) with stiffness response R ∝ k⁻⁴, demonstrates smooth transition, survival valley recovery, GR recovery, spatiotemporal localization, parameter robustness (49.6%), and fσ₈ consistency (Δχ² = −0.03).

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper establishes the first numerical demonstration that a single relativistic EFC action produces both μ < 1 in the linear cosmological regime and is compatible with μ > 1 in the non-linear Newtonian regime, connected by a smooth k^-4 stiffness transition. It reproduces the survival valley (μ ≈ 0.94, η > 1, Σ > 1) and GR recovery at high k, closing a critical conceptual gap about whether EFC's galactic and cosmological predictions are one theory or two. However, it is a T2 numerical consistency test — not analytic proof or observational validation — so it advances but does not fully close the ADM Hamiltonian stability gap or any Stage-IV kill criterion.

This suggests the graph ingestion pipeline may not have indexed earlier EFC papers referenced as [1]–[4] in the bibliography, or their concept tags are misaligned. The concept 'spatiotemporal localization' appears in the graph tags but is not explicitly discussed in the paper excerpt — it likely enters through the grid-mode BE statistics and the flow constraint. This implicit connection should be made explicit in the graph to enable future traversal from microphysics papers.

The concept 'regime transition' is central and should become a hub node connecting galactic-scale tests (rotation curves, RAR) to cosmological-scale tests (CMB lensing, RSD, fσ8) — this paper provides the theoretical bridge that the graph currently lacks.

implicit_consequences: The k^-4 scaling is a falsifiable spectral signature: EFCLASS or any Boltzmann solver implementing this must reproduce exactly k^-4 and not k^-2 or k^-6 — this constrains the EFCLASS development (theory-efclass-boltzmann-solver gap).

The sealed prediction P1 (μeff ≈ 1.1, Σeff ≈ 1.2 at cluster scales k ~ 0.3 h/Mpc) creates a direct confrontation point with DES Y6 and Euclid cluster lensing that does not yet appear in the active test pipeline — a new pipeline test should be planned.

The sealed prediction P2 (no μ > 1 in the linear regime) makes the DESI DR2 fσ8 pipeline (current biggest gap) even more critical: if DESI measures fσ8 implying μ > 1 at linear scales, EFC is killed by its own KC1.

The explicit acknowledgment that the rigorous derivation of Eq.(5) from the action is unavailable (Section 7.2d) means the micro→macro bridge is still a theoretical gap — this is adjacent to but distinct from the ADM Hamiltonian stability gap and may warrant its own gap entry.

The calibrated parameters (Table 1: α = 0.001, K_bar = 643, etc.) are now committed values — any future EFCLASS run or analytic calculation must be consistent with these or explain deviations, creating an internal consistency constraint across the paper series.

The paper's kill criteria KC1–KC5 are paper-specific and partially overlap with but are distinct from the project-level KC1–KC5. The project dashboard should clarify this to avoid confusion — the paper KC3 (k^-4 scaling rejection) and KC4 (GR recovery failure) are new falsifiability conditions not previously explicit at project level.
